basic_details.job_title: DSIR Junior Technical Assistant Recruitment 2026 - Apply Offline
basic_details.organization_name: Department of Scientific and Industrial Research (DSIR), Ministry of Science and Technology
basic_details.short_information: Department of Scientific and Industrial Research (DSIR) Junior Technical Assistant (JTA) Draft Recruitment Rules 2026 have been released on 27 July 2026 on the official DSIR website. A total of 5 (subject to variation) Junior Technical Assistant vacancies have been proposed through the draft Recruitment Rules.

important_dates.raw: Notice/Draft Rules published: 27 July 2026 Comment window for stakeholders: 30 days from the date of publication of the notice Recruitment notification, application start date, and last date: Not available yet - DSIR has not issued an actual recruitment/vacancy notification at this stage

age_limit.details: Maximum age for direct recruits: Not exceeding 30 years Age relaxation: Relaxable for Government servants up to five years, in accordance with instructions or orders issued by the Central Government Crucial date for age calculation: The closing date for receipt of applications - and not the extended closing date allowed for candidates from remote areas such as Assam, Meghalaya, Arunachal Pradesh, Mizoram, Manipur, Nagaland, Tripura, Sikkim, Lahaul and Spiti District, Pangi Sub-Division of Chamba District (Himachal Pradesh), and the Union Territories of Ladakh, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, and Lakshadweep Age limit for deputation appointment: Not exceeding 56 years, as on the closing date for receipt of applications

qualification.details: As per column 7 of Schedule I, direct recruits must hold one of the following: | A Bachelor's degree from a recognised university or institute in a discipline specified in Schedule II of the rules, or A three-year Diploma in Engineering/Technology from a recognised university or institute | Candidates with a postgraduate background in life sciences, biotechnology, agriculture, or related science disciplines fall under the eligible discipline groups listed above, provided the qualifying degree specifies the relevant subject as the main discipline.

salary_details.classification: General Central Service, Group B, Non-Gazetted, Non-Ministerial
salary_details.details: The notice does not break down allowances (DA, HRA, TA) separately, so only the pay matrix level is confirmed at this stage.

selection_process: The draft rules do not specify a written-exam or interview scheme for direct recruitment through SSC (this will follow SSC's own recruitment process once the rules are finalised and a vacancy notification is issued). For confirmation/selection matters
the rules specify a Departmental Selection/Confirmation Committee comprising:
Scientist not below the rank of Scientist 'F' - Chairman Deputy Secretary or Under Secretary in charge of Establishment - Member Scientist not below the rank of Scientist 'C' - Member
Consultation with the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) is not applicable under this post's rules.
how_to_apply: Not available yet. This notice only publishes the draft Recruitment Rules for stakeholder comments; it does not open applications. Once the rules are finalised, actual recruitment for JTA posts will be conducted through the Staff Selection Commission (SSC), which will separately publish the application process, portal link, and dates.
important_instructions: This is a draft notification of Recruitment Rules, issued under DoPT O.M. No. AB-14017/61/2008-Estt.(RR) dated 13 October 2015, which requires draft rules to be published for 30 days to invite stakeholder comments before finalisation. These draft rules supersede the DSIR Junior Technical Assistant (Group 'C' post) Recruitment Rules, 1996, except for matters already done or omitted before this supersession. Stakeholders wishing to comment on the draft rules should do so within 30 days from the date of publication of the notice (27 July 2026). The rules will come into force on the date of their publication in the Official Gazette, after finalisation. The notice was issued by Jayant Kumar, Under Secretary to the Government of India, with a request to Dr. D. R. Das, Scientist 'E', DSIR, to upload the draft rules on the department's website.

Candidates possessing a Bachelor's degree in Science or a Diploma in Engineering/ Technology may also explore more Graduate Government Jobs and Diploma Government Jobs available in Delhi. Candidates interested in scientific and technical government careers can also check the latest Central Government Jobs and Science & Technology Jobs matching their qualifications. Those looking for upcoming vacancies through the Staff Selection Commission can browse the latest SSC Recruitment Notifications for future Junior Technical Assistant and other technical posts.

content_sections.heading: DSIR JTA Recruitment 2026 - Vacancy Details
content_sections.text: The Schedule I annexed to the draft rules specifies the following post: The vacancy figure of 5 posts is marked with a footnote in the rules stating it may vary depending on workload; no category-wise (UR/SC/ST/OBC) reservation breakup has been published in this notice.

content_sections.heading: DSIR JTA Recruitment 2026 - Eligibility Criteria
content_sections.text: Eligibility under the draft rules covers age, educational qualification, and a general disqualification clause: Age limit: not exceeding 30 years for direct recruits (see age limit section below) Educational qualification: a recognised Bachelor's degree in a specified science discipline, or a three-year Diploma in Engineering/Technology (see qualification section below) General disqualification: a person who has a living spouse and marries again, or marries a person who already has a living spouse, is not eligible for appointment - unless the Central Government grants an exemption where such a marriage is permissible under the applicable personal law

content_sections.heading: DSIR JTA Recruitment 2026 - Educational Qualification
content_sections.text: As per column 7 of Schedule I, direct recruits must hold one of the following: A Bachelor's degree from a recognised university or institute in a discipline specified in Schedule II of the rules, or A three-year Diploma in Engineering/Technology from a recognised university or institute Candidates with a postgraduate background in life sciences, biotechnology, agriculture, or related science disciplines fall under the eligible discipline groups listed above, provided the qualifying degree specifies the relevant subject as the main discipline.

rows.includes: Physics, Physics (Electronics), Applied Physics, Solid State Physics, Computational Physics, Engineering Physics, Physics and Electronics, Basic Sciences with specialisation in Physics, and other disciplines with Physics as the main subject
Chemistry, Organic Chemistry, Inorganic Chemistry, Analytical Chemistry, Physical Chemistry, Applied Chemistry, Chemical Sciences, and other disciplines with Chemistry as the main subject
Biology, Life Sciences, Biotechnology Sciences, and other disciplines with Biology or Biotechnology as the main subject

Geology and Geophysics, Geology, Applied Geology, Marine Sciences, Meteorology, Oceanography and Coastal Area Studies, Physical Oceanography, Geo-informatics, Marine Geophysics, Geology and Mineralogy, Earth Sciences, Geophysics, Applied Geophysics, and related disciplines
Environment and Ecology, Environment, Ecology, and related disciplines
Mathematics, Applied Mathematics, Mathematics and Computing, Mathematical Sciences, and related disciplines
Computational Science, Data Science, Statistics, Computational Statistics, Information Science, Applied Statistics, Cryptography, and related disciplines
Agriculture, Agricultural Physics, Agricultural Chemistry, Agricultural Engineering, Agricultural Microbiology, Vegetable Science, and related disciplines

faq.question: Q1. Is DSIR JTA Recruitment 2026 open for applications now?
faq.answer: No. As of the 27 July 2026 notice, DSIR has only published draft Recruitment Rules for the JTA post for stakeholder comments. No application window is open yet.

faq.question: Q2. How many DSIR Junior Technical Assistant posts are there?
faq.answer: The draft rules specify 5 posts, marked as subject to variation depending on workload.

faq.question: Q3. What is the age limit for DSIR JTA?
faq.answer: Not exceeding 30 years for direct recruits, with up to 5 years' relaxation for Government servants as per Central Government instructions.

faq.question: Q4. What qualification is required for DSIR Junior Technical Assistant?
faq.answer: A recognised Bachelor's degree in a science discipline listed in Schedule II, or a three-year Diploma in Engineering/Technology from a recognised university or institute.

faq.question: Q5. What is the pay level for DSIR JTA?
faq.answer: Level-6 in the pay matrix, corresponding to Rs. 35,400–112,400.

faq.question: Q6. How will DSIR JTA recruitment be conducted?
faq.answer: Through direct recruitment via the Staff Selection Commission (SSC), with a separate deputation route used only for filling short-term vacancies.

faq.question: Q7. Where can I submit comments on the draft DSIR JTA Recruitment Rules?
faq.answer: The notice states that stakeholders may furnish comments within 30 days of publication; the notice does not specify an email address or portal for submission, so applicants should check the DSIR website for the submission channel.
